messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Dutch, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Dutch line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Ik werd geboren onder Julio hoewel het laat was, en ik leefde in Rome onder de goede Augustus in de tijd van de valse en leugenachtige goden.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------|-------------------|--------| | Nacqui | “I was born” (1st sg perfect) | **werd geboren** | “was born” | OK | | sub | preposition “under” (temporal/political) | **onder** | “under” | OK | | Iulio | proper name, the ruler/era | **Julio** | “Julio” | OK | | ancor | concessive adverb “although” | **hoewel** | “although” | OK | | che | subordinator introducing subjunctive clause | – (absorbed in “hoewel”) | – | **UNNECESSARY** | | fosse | subjunctive “was” (state of lateness) | **was** | “was” | OK | | tardi | adjective “late” (degree) | **laat** | “late” | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | **en** | “and” | OK | | vissi | “I lived” (1st sg perfect) | **leefde** | “lived” | OK | | a | preposition “in/at” (location) | **in** | “in” | OK | | Roma | proper name “Rome” | **Rome** | “Rome” | OK | | sotto | preposition “under” (political authority) | **onder** | “under” | OK | | ’l | definite article “the” (masc. sing.) | **de** | “the” | OK | | buono | adjective “good” (positive evaluation) | **goede** | “good” | OK | | Augusto | proper name “Augustus” | **Augustus** | “Augustus” | OK | | nel | contraction “in the” (temporal) | **in** | “in” | OK | | tempo | noun “time” (epoch) | **tijd** | “time” | OK | | de | preposition “of” (genitive) | **van** | “of” | OK | | li | definite article “the” (masc. pl.) | **de** | “the” | OK | | dèi | noun “gods” (plural) | **goden** | “gods” | OK | | falsi | adjective “false” (attribute) | **valse** | “false” | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | **en** | “and” | OK | | bugiardi | adjective “lying” (attribute) | **leugenachtige** | “lying” | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: **che** – the Italian subordinator is not needed in Dutch because the concessive meaning is fully expressed by “hoewel”.
No other source tokens are missing, wrong, or grammatically mismatched.
